errors.problem: unvocalised أحمل covers أَحْمِلُ 'I carry' (Form I, the basic beginner sense) as well as أُحَمِّلُ 'I download' (Form II); the gloss gives only the Form II sense. Same for حملت = I downloaded (حَمَلْتُ 'I carried', حَمَلَتْ 'she carried', حَمَلْتَ 'you carried')
errors.fix: أحمل → 'I carry; I download'; حملت → 'I carried, I downloaded (also: you carried / she carried)'

errors.problem: أقدم also spells أُقَدِّمُ 'I present, I offer, I apply' (Form II, very common in a course that teaches تقديم / أتقدم); the 'before a noun' note is sentence-specific and the comparative sense 'older' is missing
errors.fix: older, oldest; I present, I offer (I apply)

errors.current: الدين = al-Din (second part of the name: 'of the faith')
errors.problem: الدين is first of all the common noun 'the religion' (الدِّين); the gloss only gives the name-component sense, so a learner tapping الدين in any other sentence learns a wrong meaning
errors.fix: the religion; al-Din (second part of names such as Salah al-Din: 'of the faith')

errors.problem: الضيق also spells الضَّيِّق 'the narrow (m)' (the glossary itself has الضيقة = the narrow (f)); a learner tapping الشارع الضيق gets 'hardship'
errors.fix: the narrow (m); hardship, a hard time (ḍīq)

errors.problem: العام is above all 'the year' (العَام, e.g. العام الماضي); the gloss gives only the adjective sense
errors.fix: the year; the general, the public (adjective)

errors.problem: الحساب also means 'the (bank) account' (the glossary has حسابا = an account, حسابك = your account); in a bank scene the gloss 'the bill' is wrong
errors.fix: the bill; the account

errors.problem: جد is first of all 'grandfather' (جَدّ; the glossary has جدك, جدته, جدهم, الجد); the verb sense alone is wrong wherever the noun appears (e.g. جد سامي)

errors.problem: جمع also spells جَمْع 'plural' (the course teaches الجمع = the plural, جمع المذكر …) and 'gathering'; the verb-only gloss is wrong in every grammar context
errors.fix: plural (grammar); gathering; (he) gathered, collected

errors.problem: جملا also spells جُمَلًا 'sentences' (accusative plural of جملة, a core grammar word in the course); a learner tapping اكتب جملا gets 'a camel'
errors.fix: sentences (object form); a camel (object form)

errors.current: حرب = Harb (part of a street name in Cairo)

errors.fix: war; Harb (part of a Cairo street name)

errors.problem: unvocalised رجل covers رَجُل 'man' and رِجْل 'leg, foot' (the glossary has رجلي = my leg); رجلان = two legs likewise covers رَجُلان 'two men'
errors.fix: رجل → 'man; leg, foot'; رجلان → 'two men; two legs'

errors.problem: درسنا equally spells دَرَسْنَا 'we studied' (a basic past-tense form that certainly occurs in the course); the noun-only gloss is a wrong meaning there
errors.fix: our lesson; we studied

errors.problem: أنظف also spells أُنَظِّفُ 'I clean' (the course has سأنظف = I will clean); the comparative-only gloss is wrong in that use
errors.fix: cleaner (comparative); I clean

errors.problem: wrong person: زَارَنَا is 3rd m. singular + 'us' ('he visited us'); 'they visited us' would be زارونا

errors.path: تخف; تأخذها; تحاول; تركض; تسجل; تشتر; تشتريا; تعط; تعطها; تغضبي; تقلقي; تقولوا; تنس; تنسي; تنم; تقرؤوا; تصفحوا
errors.problem: imperative/present mix-up: these are 2nd-person present/jussive forms (تَخَفْ 'you fear', تَأْخُذُها 'you take it / she takes it', تَنْسَ 'you forget'…) taken from لا + jussive prohibitions ('don't be afraid', 'don't forget'); glossed as bare imperatives they read as commands meaning the opposite of the sentence, and they are wrong wherever the same spelling is an ordinary 'you/she …' statement (تحاول = you try / she tries; تأخذها; تسجل; تركض)
errors.fix: gloss as 'you … (jussive form, used after lā = don't …)' and, where the spelling also fits the indicative, add '/ she …': e.g. تخف → 'you fear, you are afraid (after lā: don't be afraid)'; تنس → 'you forget (after lā: don't forget)'; تأخذها → 'you take it (f) / she takes it'; تحاول → 'you try / she tries'; تغضبي → 'you (f) get angry (after lā: don't get angry)'; تقولوا → 'you (all) say (after lā / an)'

errors.problem: systematic wrong person/gender: every present or future verb with the تـ prefix spells both 'you (m. sg.)' and 'she / it (f.)' (تَدْرُسُ = you study / she studies; سَتُحِبُّ = you will love / she will love); the auto glosses pick one side from a single sentence ('you … (to a man)' or '(she) …'), so a beginner tapping هي تدرس gets 'you study (to a man)' and tapping أنت تبيع gets 'she sells'. Also تدخل = '(they, f) enter', تخلع/تطفأ/تعطيك '(they) …' give only the non-human-plural reading; تصنع/تفتح give only the passive
errors.fix: generate both readings for every تـ-prefixed present/future verb: 'you (m) … / she (it) …', e.g. تدرس → 'you study (to a man) / she studies'; تبيع → 'she sells / you sell (to a man)'; تبدو → 'you look, you seem (to a man) / she (it) looks'; ستحب → 'you will love (to a man) / she will love'; ستأتي → 'she will come / you will come (to a man)'; تقل → 'she says / you say (jussive)'; تدخل → 'you enter / she enters (they, things, enter)'; تصنع → 'you make / she makes; (it, f) is made'; تعطيك → '(she, it) gives you'. The bare 'you …' glosses (تترك, تحكي, تشاهد, تفكر, تنام, تمشي, تستمر …) need the same '/ she …' addition

errors.fix: generate 'I … / you … / (she …)' for every past ـت form, e.g. رأيت → 'I saw / you saw'; رأيته → 'I saw it (m) / you saw it'; اشتريت → 'I bought / you bought'; حجزت → 'she booked / I booked / you booked'; حصلت → 'you got / I got / she got'; أخطأت → 'you made a mistake / I made a mistake'; أكلته → 'I ate it / you ate it'; زارته → 'she visited him / I visited him'; اتفقت → 'she agreed / I agreed / you agreed' (and drop the note '-i links to the next word')

summary: Checked all ~1,700 auto-glossary entries (آتي … سيارتي) as spelling-level dictionary glosses that must hold wherever the unvocalised word appears. 20 major findings and 15 minor findings (several grouped). The dominant pattern is one-sidedness inherited from a single source sentence: (1) every تـ-prefixed present/future verb is glossed as either 'you (m)' or 'she' though the spelling is both; (2) every past ـت verb is glossed as only I, only you or only she; (3) ـك suffixes carry a fixed 'to a man / to a woman' tag; (4) Form II/III/V/VIII/X imperatives and 3ms past share a spelling but get one gloss, and Form IV 1s present vs 3ms past likewise; (5) prohibitions were stripped of لا and glossed as bare imperatives (تخف = 'be afraid'). Beyond these, 15 individual keys give a one-sentence sense while a basic beginner meaning of the same spelling is missing (رجل leg, جد grandfather, جمع plural, جملا sentences, الدين religion, العام year, درسنا we studied, الضيق narrow, الحساب account, حرب war, أحمل carry, أقدم I present, أنظف I clean), one wrong person (زارنا), one wrong leaked alternative (خالتك 'your cousin'), and ~70 glosses with sentence-specific syntax notes or contradictory quoted tenses leaked into the dictionary text.
